about: File search's grammar, plugins/filesearch/query.lua parse, the rules its header states. A dot attached to a token is a type when the name after it is a type, a lone dot asks for hidden paths and a lone bang for ignored ones, and these are read only in the leading slot, in any order, until a token is none of them. The first token left that holds a slash is the scope, split at its last slash, and the rest is the text, whitespace collapsed. A text starting with a dot asks for hidden paths when no type was read. kind is recent with nothing to search, browse with a scope and no text, search otherwise. types is a small table of its own, so a change to config/filesearch.lua never moves these. An expect field left out is not checked.

cases.name: an empty field is the recent list
spaces only are the recent list
a dot attached to a known type filters by it
a lone dot asks for hidden paths and is no type
a bare word is never a type
a dotted name that is no type is a hidden filename
a type is read case folded
sigils and types combine in any order before a scope
a type given twice counts once
two types join their extensions in the order typed
a lone bang asks for ignored paths
every leading sigil and a type together
a scope token splits at its slash and the rest is text
a scope with nothing after it is a browse
a scope splits at its last slash
a slash later in the text is not a scope
a type after the scope is text, since types are read only before it
a type before the scope filters it
whitespace in the text collapses
a dotted filename asks for hidden paths with no sigil
a dotted text after a type does not ask for hidden paths
a lone dot with nothing else is the recent list with hidden paths
a lone bang with nothing else is the recent list with ignored paths
a bare type with nothing else is the recent list, filtered
a root slash is a browse of the root
a deep scope ending in a slash is a browse
two dots and a type name is no type
a scope and text outside ASCII
raw is kept untouched
